Run a dplyr verb on the CPU and re-upload the result

Source: R/fallback.R
gpu_fallback.Rd

The core CPU fallback primitive. Materializes any pending lazy operations, collects .data to a tibble (restoring group_by() structure from .data$groups so grouped semantics apply on the CPU exactly as they would on a real grouped_df; a rowwise table becomes dplyr's rowwise_df of its rowwise vars), applies expr_fn (which should call the real dplyr verb), and re-uploads the result via tbl_gpu() (a rowwise_df result goes back up as a rowwise table).

Usage

gpu_fallback(
  verb_name,
  .data,
  expr_fn,
  ...,
  as_is = FALSE,
  detail = NULL,
  reason = detail,
  expr = NA_character_,
  also = NULL
)

Arguments

verb_name

Character, the verb name to use in the fallback notification (e.g. "transmute", "slice_min"), gated by options(cuplyr.fallback = ) (see cuplyr_fallback_notify()).

.data

A tbl_gpu object.

expr_fn

A function of one argument (a tibble, already grouped if .data was grouped) that calls the corresponding real dplyr verb and returns its result.

as_is

Logical. If TRUE, expr_fn's return value is always returned unchanged, never re-uploaded – for a verb that returns metadata about the grouping/data rather than a transformed dataset, even when that metadata happens to be a small data frame (dplyr's own grouping-metadata queries, e.g. group_data()/group_keys(), are GPU-native and don't use it; the parameter is for any fallback verb with the same "always a plain R object" shape).

detail

Older spelling of reason.

reason

Text saying why the call runs on the CPU: the reason of the notice (cuplyr_fallback_notify(), cuplyr-fallback). Every caller gives one; a reason made by fallback_failed_reason() or shadow_screen_text() carries the offending expression as its "expr" attribute. On a rowwise table it is prefixed with "rowwise table: " (rowwise_rerun() passes the reason its native attempt recorded).

expr

The offending expression as text, when the whole call is not at fault (NA: the call as a whole goes).

also

A second tbl_gpu (the y of a join, set operation or rows_*(); or a list of them) the fallback collects too: its size is added to the notice. It must not have pending operations (compute it first).

Value

Either a new tbl_gpu (grouping, execution mode, and factor levels restored/round-tripped), or expr_fn's raw return value unchanged when: as_is = TRUE; the result isn't a data frame at all (e.g. group_map()'s list); or the result is a data frame that contains list-columns (e.g. nest_by()/group_nest()/ nest_join()'s nested-tibble columns), which have no GPU representation.

When the result is a grouped data frame whose group_data() keeps groups with no row that a plain regroup of its data would not have (dplyr's dplyr_col_modify.grouped_df() does this for a verb that leaves the group columns alone, after filter()/slice() with .preserve = TRUE), the returned tbl_gpu carries those keys as $fixed_keys (see fixed_keys_of()); verbs that regroup get none.

Details

The lazy result of a lazy .data carries the step's history as its origin field (fallback_record_origin()), which explain() and show_query() print.
